messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a 18% throughput drop and a 2.1GB/km memory spike on nf4 downstream after yesterday's autoscaler tuning. Starts around 2419998870. p95 token latency jumped from 48ms -> 78ms.
sam: ugh. which change specifically? the scale-in hysteresis tweaks? :thinking_face:
devin: yeah we lowered the min-batch window and reduced node hold time to 30s. I thought it would reduce cost, not thrash kernels.
maria: timeline: 2419998870 autoscaler applied config v2.3.4, 2419998880 kernel selector started preferring nf4-compact-kernel on small batches, 2419998895 memory thrash alerts.
lee: can you paste the logs? any OOMs or slab failures?
maria: logs snippet: `2026-03-18T12:01:05Z runtime INFO kernel_select: chosen=nf4-compact-kernel batch_size=8 seq_len=64 p95=42ms`
maria: then `2026-03-18T12:01:55Z runtime WARN kv_cache: slab_alloc_fail count=14 free_frag=0.08 total_free=120MiB`
devin: slab_alloc_fail + small batches -> fragmentation. The compact kernel uses a different allocator layout.
sam: does fp4 show same?
maria: FP4 hosts didn't spike. Only nodes running nf4-compact. FP4 used mixedbatch-kernel which kept larger contiguous KV slabs.
ops_oncall: incidentbot: memory-usage-high on cluster inference-prod-nf4-2 (pager sent) :rotating_light:
lee: interesting — autoscaler reduced node hold so kernels were hot-swapping between nf4-compact and nf4-standard more frequently. That increases KV evictions and creates fragmentation.
devin: might also be kernel code path: nf4-compact uses aggressive per-layer quant buffers that are freed/realloced each request, small windows amplify cost.
maria: repro command if you want to run a synthetic load: `wrk -t4 -c200 --lua gen_chat.lua http://nf4-canary.local/generate` with `--seq 64 --batch 8`
sam: running now on canary.
sam: p95 on canary matches: 46ms -> 70ms when autoscale=fast. Memory curve shows sawtooth.
lee: quick mitigation: revert autoscaler hold-time to 120s and re-enable kernel affinity for >16 batch fallback to nf4-standard. Should reduce oscillation.
devin: also add a heuristics guard: if slab_free < 200MiB then force kernel_fallback=standard for next 60s.
maria: agree. We should also capture profiling traces: `TRACE=kernel,kv_gc ./profiling/run_profile.sh --samples 30` and upload to perfdash.
ops_oncall: infra-bot: created ticket INF-7842: "nf4 autoscale/kernel interference - memory fragmentation" assigned to eng-runtime.
sam: note: calibration sweep last week adjusted quant scaling for nf4 to reduce loss; could be slightly different alignment causing extra per-layer buffer. Not sure it would cause memory leak but worth checking.
lee: good point. Can we diff the calibration artifacts used by compact vs standard? Path: `/models/nf4/calibrations/v3/compact/summary.json` vs `/models/nf4/calibrations/v3/standard/summary.json`
maria: grabbing diffs now. The compact profile increased per-head scale by ~1.2x on some layers.
devin: rounding in quant kernels can change internal temporary buffer sizes when fused ops choose different tiling. This is plausible.
sam: action list: 1) revert autoscale hold-time (maria) 2) add slab_free guard + kernel fallback (devin) 3) run profiling traces and upload (sam) 4) diff calibration artifacts and run calibration backtest for nf4-compact (lee) 5) monitor canary for 2 hours, then decide rollback to previous kernel rollout if stable.
maria: rolling back autoscaler config now. patch: `kubectl apply -f autoscaler/hold-time-120s.yaml` :white_check_mark:
sam: started profiling, uploading to perfdash -> https://perf.redwood.example/dash/INF-7842 :eyes:
devin: I'll open a small canary PR to add the slab_free guard in kernel selector: `pr#4567`
lee: if we still see edge spikes, plan B is to disable nf4-compact from the model catalog for hosted until we vet kernels.
maria: agreed. Also add a short-term metric: kernel-switch-rate per node so we can alert on thrash.
sam: postmortem note: autoscaler cost optimization regressed performance; need explicit perf safety net for kernel-sensitive changes.
maria: thanks all. will update INF-7842 with traces and next checks at +30m and +2h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ops_oncall: incidentbot: alert cleared on cluster inference-prod-nf4-2 at 2419998922
maria: canary stabilization looks good at +12m. p95 back within 5% of baseline. leaving ticket open for calibration diffs and selector patches. :thumbsup:
